testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: At what psi does the safety valve open?
questions.explanation: The safety valve on the first air tank opens at 150 psi. This releases air if pressure gets too high. If the valve opens, there is a system problem that needs repair.

questions.question: When inspecting a coupling under the trailer, you should:

options.text: Detach the jaws from around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking lever is in the "emergency" position.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: Look into the back of the fifth wheel. Check that the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: What is a bobtail?

options.text: A tractor that goes faster than the speed limit
A tractor that goes slower than the speed limit

questions.explanation: A bobtail is a tractor without a semi-trailer. Drivers must use extra caution when operating a bobtail tractor.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, position the tractor:

options.text: Directly in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor directly in front of the trailer. Backing at an angle could cause the trailer to move and damage the landing gear.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in S-cam brakes, air pressure pushes the rod and moves the:
questions.explanation: Air enters the brake chambers when you press the brake pedal. The pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: At speeds under 40 mph, keep at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of vehicle length.
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow one second of space for every 10 feet of vehicle length. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: Which color marks emergency air lines on glad hands?
questions.explanation: Color-coded trailer air lines use blue for service lines and red for emergency lines.

questions.question: Which vehicle type is most prone to the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Triple combination trailers are most likely to experience the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to function.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems use compressed air to work properly.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning signal turns on while driving, you should:

options.text: Exit the road and park as soon as safely possible.
Stop where you are and park.
Put on your hazard lights and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the road and park as soon as safely possible.
questions.explanation: Safely exit the roadway and park as soon as possible. If air pressure gets too low, your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: What happens when a trailer's wheels lock up?
questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, the trailer tends to swing around. This can cause a jackknife.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
When the vehicle in front is moving too slowly.
When a truck driver is driving too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a vehicle is driven too fast. To reduce rollover risk, keep cargo weight low to the ground and drive slowly on turns and curves.

questions.question: What happens if air tank pressure drops below 60 psi?

options.text: A warning light will turn on.
The vehicle will not shift gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning light will turn on.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, a warning signal activates if air tank pressure drops below 60 psi. The signal may be a warning light or a wig wag.

questions.question: What is true about combination vehicles?

options.text: They often have taller trailers than single vehicles.
They are usually lighter than single vehicles.
They require more skill to drive than single vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They require more skill to drive than single vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more skill to drive. They are longer, heavier, and more at risk of rollover than single vehicles.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The trailer service air line is also called the control line or signal line.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure activates a switch and:

options.text: Turns on the low pressure warning light.
Turns off the low pressure warning light.

questions.explanation: In an air brake vehicle, pressing the brake pedal sends air pressure to an electric switch. This switch turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle usually requires ____ driving a single vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more skill to drive. They are longer, heavier, and more at risk of rollover.

questions.question: To help prevent a rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Placed as high as possible inside the trailer.
Placed as low as possible inside the trailer.
Placed on the passenger side of the trailer.
Placed on the driver's side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Placed as low as possible inside the trailer.
questions.explanation: To reduce rollover risk, keep cargo weight as low to the ground as possible. Do not place weight mainly on one side, as this makes the trailer lean and increases rollover risk.

questions.question: What color are ABS malfunction lamps?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow malfunction lamps.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, you should:
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, shift into a low gear. Gravity will speed up your vehicle as you go downhill.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to operate?
questions.explanation: Large trucks often use air brakes. Air brakes use compressed air to work.

questions.question: If a trailer starts to skid, what should the driver do?
questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes. This lets the wheels grip the road again. Once the wheels have traction, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that moves air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes when used
A part that allows air to move freely in the braking unit

questions.explanation: A wig wag warns drivers of low air pressure in an air brake system. It drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when air pressure falls below 60 psi.

questions.question: What happens if a trailer is too high?
questions.explanation: Before coupling a tractor and trailer, check the trailer height. If the trailer is too low, the nose may be damaged. If it is too high, it may not couple correctly.

questions.question: What color identifies service lines on air brake hoses?
questions.explanation: Air hoses are sometimes color-coded to help drivers avoid mistakes when connecting glad hands. Blue identifies service lines. Red identifies emergency lines.
